description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects - Increased Access to Finance for Microenterprises, Including Women, Agri, and Rural Entrepreneurs: The project is expected to increase access to finance for microenterprises in Kazakhstan, including women entrepreneurs and agribusinesses in rural areas. Despite recent growth, access to finance for MSMEs remains constrained by factors such as high interest rates, high perceived risk of lending to this segment, a high reliance on immovable collateral as a pledge against loanswhich MSMEs often lackand a lack of tailored loan products, particularly for entrepreneurs in rural areas. According to the forthcoming MSME Finance Gap data, Kazakhstan is facing a significant finance gap for MSMEs, estimated at US$16.9 billion, equivalent to 10.15% of GDP. The gap for women-owned MSMEs is estimated at US$4.9 billion. 29.9% of MSMEs in Kazakhstan are credit constrained, and only 17.2% of firms have access to bank loans and or line of credit. Furthermore, there is a significant rural gap in terms of financial inclusion and consumer finance. The project will support the growth of a microfinance institution with a strong focus on targeting women and rural agri entrepreneurs who remain underserved in the market.
Market effect - Competitiveness: The Project will support competitiveness in the market by strengthening the capacity and supporting the growth of a second tier Agri MSME lender in the market. In an increasingly competitive financial sector, the project is expected to support sustaining the traditional MFI sector that lends to Agri/rural MSMEs, which remain underserved by both the banking sector and digital microfinance lenders.

The proposed Project consists of a senior loan of up to $5 million, to be disbursed in local currency (Kazakhstani Tenge or KZT), to microfinance organization Asian Credit Fund LLC (ACF or the Company). ACF will use the proceeds from the loan to provide access to finance for underserved microenterprises (MEs) in rural areas of Kazakhstan. 75% of the proceeds are planned to be earmarked for agricultural (Agri) end-borrowers, and up to 50% for women-owned microenterprises (WMEs). IFC's loan is expected to have a tenor of up to 3 years with a 12-month grace period.
